title: Leo's Stretchy Rocket
markdown:
The sun peeked. Leo bounced out of bed, feet tapping a speedy rhythm. Today was the Science Club’s costume parade. He had built a spectacular rocket ship costume. Big and silver, with pointy fins and a sparkly nose cone.

“It’s going to be amazing!” he chirped.

But as he popped it on, the rocket costume plopped down around his ankles like a collapsed tent.

“Oh dear,” Aunt Rosa said, tying ribbons onto his helmet. “This magnificent rocket needs stability. Let’s try this pin.”

Pin. The rocket tilted. Slip. It slid right back down. Leo looked like a silver mushroom.

Fern the fawn nudged Leo. “Perhaps some sticky tape?”

Aunt Rosa grabbed a roll of strong sticky tape. Tape. They smoothed it down. It held for a second. Then, with a quiet riiip, the tape peeled away. The rocket flopped again. Leo’s bright grin started to droop.

“This is tricky!” Aunt Rosa declared.

Fern twitched her ears, then let them spring back. Snap. They stayed upright.

Leo watched. He picked up a toy car with a bright red rubbery band stretched tightly around its wheels. It looked snug and strong. It didn’t slip.

“Look!” Leo pointed. “Fern’s ears stretch. They bounce back. And the car band is so tight.” He wiggled his fingers. “What if the costume needs something that has to be stretchy, but still holds tight, like a hug?”

Aunt Rosa’s eyes twinkled. “Stretchy but strong! Brilliant, clever thought, Leo!”

Fern trotted to her basket and nudged out a bright blue sock. “This sock is very stretchy. It springs back when I pull it.”

Leo grabbed it. He cut a wide band from the sock, like the band on the toy car. He stretched it over his shoulders. It hugged the costume snug.

Wiggle. The rocket stood UP straight. Fins pointed proudly. No slippy-slippy.

“Hooray!” Leo cheered. “It works!”

Aunt Rosa clapped. “You found it, Leo. A material that stretches kindly but holds tight. Like a hug for your costume.”

Fern nodded. Leo grinned. He adjusted his silver rocket, feeling confident. “This is way better than tape or pins.”

He stood tall in the doorway. The sock band stayed a snug circle. Fern’s ears stayed up. The parade was waiting, and Leo, with a happy bounce, zoomed out, rocket ready, no mushroom, no flop.
